title: Chopin’s nocturne, five recorded perspectives
work: Nocturne in F-sharp major, Op. 15 No. 2
question: How do the older pianists and two modern recordings distribute time between song, contrast and return?
intro: The comparison places d’Albert’s 1916 recording beside Paderewski’s 1917 and 1937 accounts, then Luke Faulkner and Patrizia Prati’s modern recordings. Paderewski’s 1909 essay describes rubato as expressive flexibility, not time that must always be repaid mechanically within a bar. Prati’s live Madrid performance is dated 24 November 2015; Faulkner’s recording date is not established. Recorded amplitude and piano colour reflect different transfer chains and should not be mistaken for direct measurements of touch.
